subject: Private Runtime Observability: encrypted forwarder topology & SIEM ingestion test plan
messages:
From: Priya Shah <ops@nexabank.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: security@nexabank.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Observability for private runtime — encrypted egress and SIEM mapping

Hi Olga,

We'd like to kick off an evidence and connectivity exercise for our private Redwood runtime (VPC) ahead of production cutover. Two asks: 1) a short test plan that proves logs/metrics/traces can reach our Splunk HEC and SIEM ingest while preserving mutual-TLS (we require mTLS client auth at the edge), and 2) a network topology that shows where traffic exits our VPC and which ports/IPs need to be allowlisted.

Constraints:
- All telemetry must traverse an outbound proxy in our DMZ (we cannot open inbound ports).
- Traffic must be TLS 1.2+ with client certs; no plaintext.
- We need a minimal set of sample events that map to our SIEM schema so our SOC can validate field mapping.

Can Redwood provide a concise test plan (steps + sample payloads), an encrypted-forwarder topology diagram, and an estimate of any temporary firewall rules we should add for a short ingest test? We're trying to schedule this in the next two weeks.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform, NexaBank
pri.shah@nexabank.com
+44 20 5555 1234

[Attachment: current-siem-field-mapping.csv (csv stub)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <ops@nexabank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability for private runtime — encrypted egress and SIEM mapping

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear requirements. We're happy to own the test plan and provide the topology. Quick summary of what we'll deliver:

- A step-by-step SIEM ingest test plan with sample events and expected field mappings (PDF).
- An encrypted-forwarder topology diagram showing the forwarder, DMZ proxy, and Splunk HEC endpoints.
- Minimal port/IP allowlist for the short window (we'll provide exact CIDR and port ranges).
- Curl examples and a short validation script that uses client cert authentication to post sample events to your HEC.

To keep this scoped, can you confirm:
1) whether your DMZ proxy performs TLS termination (i.e., it holds the TLS certs) or whether it simply forwards TCP/TLS traffic to the internal endpoint?
2) the internal HEC endpoint hostname or a staging HEC we can use for the test (or we can run against a Redwood staging HEC and share sample captures).

I've attached our forwarder architecture template and a working example of a minimal event payload.

Proposed next step: 45-minute test window where we validate an end-to-end ingest and show SOC the mapping. If that's OK, please propose times and we'll coordinate.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Hi team — a few compliance-focused checks to include in the test plan (SOC2 / data custody perspective):

- Proof of encryption in transit: capture of TLS handshakes showing client cert CN, issuer, and TLS version.
- Evidence of retention policy application (sample event showing retention TTL headers if applicable).
- Access logs for the forwarder showing requestor identity and timestamps (preferably signed logs).
- Chain-of-custody note: describe where temporary logs live during the ingest test and who has access.

Operational notes:
- Allowlist: we'll need to provide your network team with an exact outbound IP/CIDR list for the test window. Keep the list as small as possible.
- If the DMZ proxy terminates TLS for you, we need the proxy cert chain to confirm trust paths; otherwise we'll use mTLS end-to-end.

I'm happy to join the call with SOC if they want to review the artifacts live.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Technical draft (topology + sample commands):

Topology (ASCII):
[Redwood Runtime] (ENI) --> [Forwarder (hosted in customer subnet)] -- TLS(mTLS) --> [DMZ Proxy (TCP forwarder, optional TLS termination)] --> [Outbound NAT] --> [Splunk HEC (staging) - 10.210.77.45:8088] 

Port requirements (minimal test):
- 443/TCP (if HEC behind TLS)
- 8088/TCP (Splunk HEC default; we will confirm)
- 22/TCP (for debug tunnel only; not required for ingest)

mTLS example (curl using client cert):
curl -v 
  --cert /path/to/client.crt 
  --key /path/to/client.key 
  --cacert /path/to/ca-chain.pem 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  https://10.210.77.45:8088/services/collector/event
  -d '{"event": "sample-login", "user":"j.smith", "severity":"info"}'

Suggested tracing hook header (so we correlate traces across Redwoods runtime):
- X-Redwood-TraceId: <trace-id>
- X-Redwood-SpanId: <span-id>
- X-Forwarder-Version: 1.2.0

Sample minimal event mapping (fields we will send to match your SIEM):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_type
- user_id
- src_ip
- redwood_trace_id
- raw_message

I'll attach a draft diagram and a small script to POST 3 test events and output the HEC response codes.

— Hiro
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
